articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Accessible Ramp
articles.deck: Residents of Lower Millrace filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The plan calls for accessible ramp along Salem Drive, with work expected to start in February.
The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Carl Varga, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 20 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Margaret Eckhart, 95, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Margaret Eckhart for the many years of service to Foundry Row.
body: Margaret Eckhart died in October at home on Lilac Terrace, at the age of 95.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Kettle Hill Block Association in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foundry Row.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Pocket Park
body: To the editor: I have lived on Hollis Drive for 12 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the July meeting.
Please keep the pocket park in the budget. Many of us on Hollis Drive use it every week.

Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Hollis Drive for 12 years, and I want to say what a difference the Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. has made.
Harold Szabo, Foundry Row

articles.title: Council Tables Playground Upgrade Ordinance
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Thistle Drive disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Councilmember Yolanda Kellerman asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $48,000.
Public works estimates the work will take about 32 weeks once it starts in September.
